The SDK relies on Node's native `zlib` bindings, which follow the original zlib semantics, whereas the CLI, which defaults to Rust's `flate2` crate, actually uses a pure‑Rust port of the `miniz` library. It turns out that `miniz` does not flush the decompressed stream as cleanly at SYNC boundaries as the reference zlib implementation does, leading to partial data being held back – what we observed as a "stall". This subtle difference can also manifest as intermittent connection instability, so the flakiness we saw in some network tests is likely a side effect of the same problem.
